title: The Problem With Medical Cannabis Isn’t The Cannabis It’s The “Medical”

content_html_sanitized:
In 1972, when I first got involved in the marijuana reform movement, I had never heard of it having any medical uses. I have been blessed with good health, and many other things, but for me it was — and still is— just about freedom.

In all these decades, I have never recommended that anyone use weed, medically or otherwise. (CBD, yes). That just means that there’s more for me!

Personally, I was happy enough with just decriminalizing it, and the original black market, with hippies, was sort of fun. Unfortunately, Big Prohibition got involved and turned the black market violent. That is literally their “modus operandi”. 

Then they discovered that they had to wage war on the sick, dying and disabled, who just wouldn’t shut up about it, and were making the Narcs look bad. How rude! But they were more than up for it.

From almost exactly 25 years ago. See The Murder of Peter McWilliams -- An Indictment, Not an Obituary by Richard Cowan

Tuesday, I wrote about how the Fentanyl disaster demonstrated how the pharmaceutical system is corrupted by power. 

See Marijuana Is In Schedule One. Fentanyl Is In Schedule 2. Think About It.

Lord Acton was right: Absolute power corrupts absolutely. And the only greater power than the power of life and death, is the power to torture a person to death, just by saying No. (Remember when just saying “No” was supposed to save the children?)

I remember cancer patients telling me that they would rather have died of cancer than go through chemotherapy without having cannabis to alleviate the nausea. One told me about how he was still suffering from a herniated esophagus caused by the violent vomiting. 

Nothing subtle about it. No research needed. 

Oh yes, of course I know that some people have psychological problems with cannabis, but I also remember a young man telling me, “I haven’t tried to kill myself since I started using marijuana.” 

Exact quote. I’m not playing God. 

Speaking of playing God, yesterday I wrote about the problems British mothers have had getting medical cannabis for their desperately sick children, even after the therapeutic state acknowledged that nothing else works.

See Two Stories Twenty Eight Years Apart Tell Us Something Terrible About The Medical System

More research?

And is this about medical or political authority? The answer is obvious.

The medical establishments in most countries have actively opposed legalizing both recreational and medical cannabis, collaborating in the criminalization of their patients, while pretending to be above it all. Clean hands are essential in surgery, but absurd in politics. That’s not the way it works in the real world. 

But now that their medical advice is being ignored, they now claim that they should be given control over access to the newly legalized (over their objections) cannabis. 

They even claim to have the expertise to decide how much and which strain and which potency their patients should get, and whether it should be covered by insurance. 

Let me make clear that there really are medical doctors who have educated themselves about the medical uses of cannabis and who can be very helpful, especially for elderly patients who have not had any experience with cannabis. 

Cannabinoid medicine is a genuine specialty, but it is actually malpractice for a doctor who has not had special training to claim medical authority. 

However, these are what are called “First World” problems. No joke. 

In most of the world there are far too few doctors, and most of the people are simply too poor to afford either doctors or pharmaceutical products. The only way that most of these people can get any sort of palliative is from their gardens, and cannabis is the safest and easiest to grow. Of course, that would only be possible if cannabis is completely legal, so that they would not be in danger of being arrested, and for it to be too cheap to be worth stealing.

From 2001, Cameroon, One of the Poorest Countries in the World, Wants to Import Medical Marijuana from Canada, One of the Richest Counties in the World. Why?

But if that will work in the poorest countries, why can’t people in the advanced economies, where they have Internet access, and access to growers who actually know about the plant, just get their cannabis without paying for permission from the people who have tried to keep them from getting it for decades. 

There will still sometimes be a need for a specialist, but most of the time a budtender will probably be enough. Indeed better.

From 1998, see The Nation Magazine Quotes Dr. Lester Grinspoon Explaining Why He Thinks Only Full Legalization Will Allow Proper Access to Medical Marijuana

Physicians heal thyselves!
